macro.title: Fed Rate Outlook Tightens Amid Inflation Resilience
macro.body: Recent CPI data shows U.S. core inflation holding above 3% for a third month, prompting Fed officials to signal a possible rate hike in September. Higher rates could dampen risk assets, especially leveraged equity exposure, while supporting the Canadian dollar via capital flows.
macro.bull: If the Fed pauses, equity volatility eases and leveraged ETFs retain upside.
macro.base: Markets trade sideways as investors price in a modest 25 bps hike.
macro.bear: A surprise 50 bps hike fuels risk-off, hitting high‑beta tech and leveraged ETFs.

macro.title: CAD Strengthening on Oil Price Stabilisation
macro.body: Oil prices have steadied after the Iran‑Hormuz flare‑up, allowing the Bank of Canada to consider a modest policy tighten. A firmer CAD reduces the USD‑CAD conversion drag on the portfolio’s 68% USD exposure.
macro.bull: CAD gains improve net CAD value of USD‑denominated holdings.
macro.bull_estimate: +$8,000–$12,000 via reduced FX drag on NVDA, AAPL, etc.
macro.base: Modest CAD appreciation offsets some equity volatility.
macro.bear: A sudden CAD drop re‑exposes the portfolio to USD‑CAD conversion loss.
macro.bear_estimate: -$10,000–$15,000 via FX exposure on leveraged ETFs

macro.title: Global Trade Realignment Around Middle‑East Tensions
macro.body: Escalating US‑Iran posturing is prompting shippers to reroute cargo, modestly raising freight costs and prompting some manufacturers to diversify supply chains. The effect on broad market indices is limited but could benefit defense and logistics equities.
macro.bull: Defense stocks gain on higher order flow.
macro.bull_estimate: +$4,000–$6,000 via potential new positions in defense sector
macro.base: Trade shifts remain incremental, no material impact on portfolio.
macro.bear: Higher logistics costs compress margins for industrials.

risks.title: Leverage Decay Amplification Risk
risks.context: 49% of portfolio (~$137K CAD) in 3x leveraged ETFs (FNGU, SPXL, UDOW)
risks.body: In volatile markets, the daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs can erode value even if the underlying index is flat, magnifying losses on both the S&P and Nasdaq exposures.

risks.title: CAD/USD Conversion Drag
risks.context: 68% of holdings are USD‑denominated, current FX 1.3925 CAD per USD
risks.body: A strengthening Canadian dollar reduces the CAD value of USD assets, while any sudden CAD depreciation could increase margin requirements on leveraged positions.

risks.title: Tech Concentration Tail Risk
risks.context: Tech stocks represent ~20% of portfolio (~$56K CAD) with NVDA at a 1,776% gain
risks.body: Heavy reliance on a few high‑growth chip makers makes the portfolio vulnerable to sector‑specific setbacks such as AI demand slowdown or regulatory curbs.

news.body: The poll shows record low approval for the U.S. president, heightening political risk and likely increasing market volatility. This environment pressures high‑beta tech and leveraged ETFs in the portfolio.
news.exposure: FNGU ~$87K CAD, SPXL ~$22K CAD, NVDA ~$33K CAD, AAPL ~$15K CAD

outcomes.label: Bull

outcomes.label: Base

outcomes.label: Bear

news.body: Escalation risk could disrupt oil shipments, lifting crude prices and boosting energy equities like ENB.TO while pressuring defense contractors.
news.exposure: ENB.TO ~$12K CAD, CM.TO ~$9K CAD, RTX (not held) – potential new entry

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: Oil price rally lifts ENB and creates buying pressure on defense stocks.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Oil stabilises after brief spike; limited impact on current holdings.

outcomes.label: Bear

news.headline: Nvidia backs financing for OpenAI data centre in Ohio
news.body: NVDA’s commitment to fund a new AI data centre underscores its central role in the AI ecosystem, potentially supporting revenue growth but also increasing capital outlay exposure.
news.exposure: NVDA ~$33K CAD, related AI peers (TSM, QCOM) also in portfolio

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: Deal accelerates AI adoption, boosting NVDA and spill‑over peers.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Project proceeds as expected; earnings remain in line.

outcomes.label: Bear

picks.thesis: Chinese EV maker NIO is benefitting from renewed Chinese strategic oil reserve purchases and a softening of domestic EV subsidies, offering upside as the EV market rebounds.
picks.entry: Target entry around C$12‑13 per share; monitor quarterly delivery numbers and Chinese policy announcements.

picks.thesis: BHP's diversified commodity exposure provides a hedge against rising oil and copper prices amid Middle‑East tensions and global infrastructure spending.
picks.entry: Consider buying on pull‑backs near C$55; watch for quarterly earnings and commodity price trends.

picks.thesis: Shopify's recent partnership with major logistics providers and its push into B2B SaaS could reignite growth, adding Canadian tech exposure without FX risk.
picks.entry: Aim for C$55‑57 range; keep an eye on Q3 earnings and merchant volume trends.

strengths.text: Low cost basis on core tech holdings (e.g., NVDA) locked in at pre‑AI boom levels, providing substantial unrealised gains.
RRSP shelter protects future growth from Canadian income tax, especially valuable given the investor's upcoming non‑resident status.
High overall portfolio ROI (+83%) demonstrates effective past allocation and compounding.
Diversified currency exposure (68% USD, 32% CAD) can act as a natural hedge against CAD fluctuations.
Strategic use of FHSA funds for the GTA home purchase preserves cash flow while leveraging tax‑advantaged growth.

concerns.text: Significant cash idle in the RRSP (~C$20K) is subject to cash‑drag, reducing overall portfolio return.
Overlap between leveraged ETFs (FNGU, SPXL, UDOW) creates concentrated exposure to the same equity indices, limiting diversification.
Single‑stock tail risk: NVDA’s massive weight and recent 1,776% gain make it vulnerable to a sharp correction if AI spending moderates.
Liquidity risk in leveraged ETFs during market stress could widen bid‑ask spreads, increasing transaction costs.
Upcoming US earnings season for many tech holdings may introduce volatility that amplifies leverage decay.

strategy_short.text: Trim exposure to 3x leveraged ETFs by reallocating ~C$30K into BHP and NIO to reduce decay risk.
Implement a modest CAD/USD hedge (e.g., short CAD futures) covering ~C$50K of USD exposure to limit conversion drag.
Deploy idle RRSP cash into SHOP to add Canadian equity exposure and mitigate FX risk.

strategy_mid.text: Gradually increase exposure to renewable energy equities (e.g., Brookfield Renewable) to align with long‑term ESG trends and diversify away from pure tech.
Build a dividend‑focused Canadian core (e.g., BCE, TELUS) within the RRSP to generate stable cash flow ahead of the 2027 repatriation of non‑resident income.
Plan phased withdrawals from the FHSA for the GTA down‑payment, timing sales to coincide with lower market volatility to preserve gains.

strategy_long.text: Establish a permanent‑resident tax‑efficient retirement core using Canadian dividend aristocrats and REITs to provide income after 2030.
Allocate a portion of future contributions to real assets (e.g., infrastructure funds) to hedge inflation over the 10‑year horizon.
Consider a citizenship or residency plan that optimises CRA foreign‑tax credit treatment for the anticipated 2027 return to Canada.

daily_outlook: Today's political volatility and Middle‑East flashpoints create a mixed environment; leveraged tech bets remain attractive but watch for decay, while defensive and dividend plays can provide balance.

tax.text: RRSP contributions remain fully deductible against Canadian taxable income; ensure 2026 contribution room is maximised before the non‑resident year ends to preserve deduction potential for 2027.
Foreign tax credits can be claimed on US dividend and capital gains; maintain detailed records of foreign withholding to offset Canadian tax upon repatriation.

Any capital gains realized in the Investment account will be taxed as ordinary income in Canada; consider deferring sales of high‑gain positions (e.g., NVDA) until after the 2027 residency reset to benefit from the capital gains exemption.

macro_history.title: US Defense Spending Surge After $22.9B Raytheon Award
macro_history.body: The Department of Defense's seven‑year contract with Raytheon for Tomahawk missile production injects a sizable, recurring fiscal stimulus into the US defense sector. Higher government outlays tend to support risk‑on sentiment and can lift equities tied to aerospace and defense, while also modestly boosting the US dollar as Treasury yields rise.
macro_history.bull: If the contract spurs broader defense‑industry earnings upgrades, US equities could rally, benefitting leveraged exposure.
macro_history.base: Markets absorb the news with limited upside, keeping equity momentum steady.
macro_history.bear: If the spending boost fuels inflation concerns, the Fed may tighten faster, pressuring growth stocks and leveraged ETFs.

macro_history.title: Escalating Iran‑Hormuz Threat Tightens Global Oil Supply
macro_history.body: Iran's warning of offensive actions in the Strait of Hormuz raises the risk of shipping disruptions for a key portion of world oil trade. Historical patterns show sharp spot‑price spikes when Hormuz tension peaks, which can reverberate through energy equities and commodity‑linked assets worldwide.
macro_history.bull: Higher oil prices lift energy stocks and commodity‑linked leveraged ETFs, adding upside to the portfolio's exposure.
macro_history.base: Oil markets may price in a risk premium without a sustained supply shock.
macro_history.bear: If the threat escalates to actual closures, a sharp sell‑off in risk assets could trigger volatility spikes, hurting leveraged positions.

macro_history.title: China Re‑starts July Oil Stockpiling, Signalling Demand Resilience
macro_history.body: Beijing's decision to replenish strategic oil reserves after a month‑long pause suggests a rebound in domestic demand and a willingness to support global oil markets. The move can buoy the Chinese yuan against the CAD as trade flows improve, while also tempering global oil price spikes.
macro_history.bull: A stronger CNY reduces CAD‑USD pressure, modestly improving the FX book and supporting Canadian exporters.
macro_history.base: FX impact remains muted; markets view the stockpiling as routine.
macro_history.bear: If the stockpiling triggers higher global oil prices, the CAD could weaken further, eroding FX gains.

This shift in trade patterns may benefit certain sectors, such as technology and finance, which are heavily represented in the portfolio.
macro_history.bull: A resolution to the US-Iran tensions could lead to a surge in global trade, benefiting the portfolio's tech and finance holdings.
macro_history.base: The current trade tensions and geopolitical events are likely to continue, leading to a mixed performance for the portfolio.
macro_history.bear: An escalation of the US-Iran tensions could lead to a significant decline in global trade, negatively impacting the portfolio's performance.
